title: Reservation contiguity controller and HDR-sketch utilization reporter
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: Dedicated capacity customers observed sporadic fragmentation of reservation windows that caused short-lived throughput cliffs during tenant bursts. This PR introduces a Reservation Contiguity Controller (RCC) that consolidates adjacent reservation segments at allocation time and an HDR-sketch based Utilization Reporter to provide robust, memory-efficient percentile signals for autoscaler decisions.

What this changes: RCC enforces a best-effort contiguity policy when creating or extending reservations so that tenant burst tokens are less likely to span many small, discontinuous slots. The contiguity heuristic prefers minimizing boundary churn while respecting placement constraints and soft-commitment SLAs. The HDR-sketch reporter replaces the previous fixed-bucket sampler for per-tenant utilization percentiles (P50/P90/P99) and feeds a new utilization-summary protobuf to the autoscaler.

Compatibility and safety: All changes are opt-in behind the feature flag dedicated.rcc_enabled and telemetry.hdr_enabled. Default rollout is off for existing Dedicated clusters; the controller is safe to run in a dry-run mode (dedicated.rcc_dry_run=true) where it only emits metrics and reconciliation logs. The reporter emits both the new sketch payload and the legacy bucketed metrics to avoid alerting gaps during rollout.

Key design notes: - Contiguity is soft: RCC will not preempt higher-priority reservations to coalesce windows. It attempts best-effort compaction within the same allocation cycle. - HDR sketch chosen due to bounded memory footprint and mergeability across pools; percentiles computed server-side for autoscaler logic. - Autoscaler integration: the autoscaler now consumes sketch-aggregated percentile signals and a new continuity_score field to weigh recent fragmentation in scale decisions.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for controller reconciliation, compaction heuristics, and conflict resolution. Integration tests mock multi-tenant allocation churn showing a 37% reduction in short-lived boundary violations in the synthetic harness. E2E job added to the dedicated-lab CI that runs against a small dedicated cluster image and validates no SLA regressions under bursty load.

Rollout plan: 1) Enable telemetry.hdr_enabled in telemetry-only clusters and validate percentile stability for 48h. 2) Enable dedicated.rcc_dry_run across canary fleet and monitor continuity_score and allocation churn metrics for 72h. 3) Flip dedicated.rcc_enabled in 10% of fleets, watch tail latency and SLA events, then scale to full roll.

Checklist: - [x] RFC and Linear attached (ENG-1129) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary e2e job - [x] Backwards-compatible telemetry fallback - [x] Docs: operational runbook added to internal wiki (link: https://linear.app/internal/rcc-runbook)

Related: touches allocation/allocator/core, autoscaler/decision, telemetry/collector and the dedicated console's reservation view. Linear/PM tickets: PM-401 describes the customer SLA acceptance criteria.

Notes: This PR intentionally leaves the strict defragmentation phase out of scope (future work) and focuses on preventing fragmentation at allocation time and improving percentile signal fidelity for the autoscaler.
commits: feat(rcc): add contiguity controller and reconciliation loop; feat(telemetry): implement HDR sketch collector and gRPC exporter; perf: reduce sketch merge allocations; test: add unit and integration tests; ci: add dedicated-lab e2e pipeline
review_conversation:
Evan: Can contiguity cause suboptimal packing under heavy fragmentation?
Maya: Controller is best-effort and will not preempt existing higher-priority allocations; added unit tests to prove safe fallbacks.
Sara: Sketch memory usage concerns for large pools?
Maya: HDR sketch uses bounded 16KB per-tenant (configurable); included memory-impact smoke tests and a prometheus gauge for total-sketch-bytes.
Carlos: Autoscaler needs a smoothing window on continuity_score to avoid flip-flops.
Maya: Added 5-minute exponential smoothing in autoscaler consumer and documented rationale.
Approvals: Evan approved (LGTM), Sara approved after sketch memory clarifications, Carlos approved pending smoothing verification which passed in canary runs.
ci_details: CI matrix: unit (go test ./...), integration (sim-harness), lint (golangci-lint), e2e (dedicated-lab). Latest run: all green; e2e ran in 42m. Notable flake: one transient sim-harness timeout retried automatically.
release_notes: Add Reservation Contiguity Controller to reduce reservation fragmentation and an HDR-sketch based utilization reporter to improve percentile signals for autoscaling. Feature gated and rolled out via canary. Impact: expected smoother tenant burst behavior and improved autoscaler stability.
